tact training of the relations between the components of compound stimuli is related to the formation of equivalence-equivalence relations.
tact training of compound stimuli is a necessary condition for the emergence of analogical reasoning as evidenced by equivalence-equivalence performance.

(1) the ability to tact the relations between stimuli is related to the ability to establish analogies; (2) the ability to establish an analogy is related to the establishment of an equivalence-equivalence relation; and (3) the ability to discriminate individual components is also related to the ability of an individual to establish an equivalence-equivalence relationship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of tact training in the development of analogies.
the effects of tact training and the development of analogies.
the role of tact training in the emergence of analogical relations.

the development of relational responding is a function of the establishment of a common name and the ability of the participant to discriminate between components of the compound.

the tact training of the relations between stimuli is a necessary condition for the development of analogies.

tact training can facilitate the development of equivalence-equivalence relations.
